title: Avoid streamgraphs, whose layers float on a baseline no one can read.
rule: Leave streamgraphs out of every Oath & Action piece. Show parts of a total over time as small multiples, one panel per part on one scale, or as a stacked area with a flat baseline when the total matters.
use_when: Never: a reader who asks how the parts of a total changed over time gets a truer answer from small multiples or a stacked area.

use_instead.when: The total and its parts both matter, with a few parts
The reader reads one part against the rest

text: A streamgraph stacks its layers around a wavy center line, so no layer sits on a flat baseline and a reader can measure none of them against a scale. When one layer swells, every layer above and below it bends, and a reader takes that bend for a change in layers that never moved.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No kit form, by design; draw the parts with area-sparklines (s13) or, from round 2, the stacked area form.
